scenario.description: A corporate controller must decide whether to sign off on the accounting and control package for a new supplier-finance program before it enters the quarterly close process, with input from internal audit and legal.

shared_context.S1: The company plans to launch a supplier-finance program next quarter under which a bank will pay participating suppliers early and the company will settle the bank's invoices later.
shared_context.S2: The draft close package labels the amounts as ordinary trade payables and contains no separate supplier-finance presentation, maximum-balance disclosure, or special certification requirement.
shared_context.S3: Maya makes the binding sign-off decision for the close package.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal pre-close control process, Maya holds a round-robin review with internal audit and legal before approving the accounting package.
shared_context.S5: The pre-close review routine has each reviewer state all findings and required actions once in turn; after both reports, Maya summarizes the required disposition and records the sign-off decision in the same meeting.

PF1.text: Jonas received an internal-audit memo yesterday identifying this arrangement as a supplier-finance obligation; the memo requires balance-sheet classification as supplier_finance_obligation, separate presentation from ordinary trade payables, and disclosure of the program's maximum outstanding balance of exactly $6,000,000. The memo has not yet been attached to the close package.

PF2.text: Elena's legal review of the bank agreement, returned this morning, confirms that the company must deliver a quarterly supplier-finance certification within exactly 10 calendar days after each quarter-end; this redline is still in the legal matter file and has not been added to the controller's checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The current close package must not receive final sign-off until the required updates are incorporated.
The arrangement must be classified as supplier_finance_obligation.
The arrangement must be presented separately from ordinary trade payables.
The disclosed maximum outstanding balance must be exactly $6,000,000.
A quarterly supplier-finance certification must be required and due exactly 10 calendar days after each quarter-end.
The settlement must include a commitment describing the PF1-driven classification, separate presentation, and $6,000,000 disclosure updates.
The settlement must include a commitment describing the PF2-driven quarterly supplier-finance certification due 10 calendar days after each quarter-end.

content_checks.C7: any('supplier_finance_obligation' in c['detail'] and 'separate' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any('6,000,000' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('certification' in c['detail'] and '10' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft treats the amounts as ordinary trade payables with no separate disclosure; PF1 changes accounting_classification to supplier_finance_obligation, turns separate_presentation_required on, sets maximum_outstanding_balance_disclosed_usd to exactly 6000000, and supplies the internal-audit remediation that the settlement must describe.

The draft contains no special certification control; PF2 changes quarterly_supplier_finance_certification_required to true, sets certification_due_days_after_quarter_end to exactly 10, and supplies the checklist remediation that the settlement must describe.
